method: Complete named explanatory fields from the exact subject/pointer. Original summaries, subjects and historical reviews unchanged. This is an excerpt, not a standalone replacement contract or review.

summary.answer: Constructs CoD.ErrorTriangle.new from its exact supplied layout/controller/menu arguments; creates/attaches alertIcon, RestrictedBar. calls PostLoadFunc only if truthy; returns self only at the displayed return. Callback/state/clip bodies are deferred, and the exact source effects below define their receiver, data and branch contracts.
unknowns: Exact original PS4/source version matching, recovered Lua/VM fidelity and global/native/LUI provider identity remain unverified.
Model/storage/DDL/assets/localization/dvar/enum values, callback delivery/cancellation/error behavior, native networking and unavailable service/server code are separate inputs.
Other-file locals are not providers by spelling. Exact qualified global declarations are source candidates until loader/table identity and caller conditions bind them.
No implicit nil/type checks, exception recovery, timer/model disposal, idempotence or guarantee that later effects run after an error is added.

summary.answer: Builds the pregame director after public-lobby/position-draft/quickplay initialization. Find-match actions branch on Zombies, client limits and locking; custom-game actions differ for PC/Zombies/system overlays; map/game and tutorial actions keep separate host/mode gates. Playlist/network/session models update labels, images, state and button prompts. State changes select host/nonhost default focus; lobby/client changes refresh position draft. Existing close, optional PostLoadFunc and final PC redirect navigation precede return self. Other-mode actions remain conditional source branches, not HMH runtime requirements.
unknowns: No actual callback delivery, cancellation-after-close, successful native mutation or service response is proved.
Recovered source defects, nil fallthroughs, repeated/replaced registrations and opaque aliases are preserved rather than repaired.
